findings.note: Portrait keeps a fixed portraitCardW (ContentView.swift:53) and the tableau never scrolls (comment at ContentView.swift:50-51), so a growing column just runs off the bottom of the screen. Landscape already solves exactly this by shrinking cardW to the current tallest column (ContentView.swift:62-73) - portrait needs the same clamp (or a smaller fan/overlap) once 30*(N-1)+75 exceeds the available board height. Long alternating runs in one column are normal Causeway play, so this is reachable in ordinary play, not just a stress test. Undo is the only recovery; a player who keeps stacking simply loses access to those cards. Inference (untested): with the Daily objectives HUD on screen the tableau starts ~40-50 pt lower, so clipping would begin ~1.5 cards earlier.

repro: launch (fresh install, Won 0)

tap the 'Clear' pill under 'Show me how to win:' (deal #10,004)

findings.note: TRAP (metric-integrity): Stop mid-demo leaves the app's own solution moves on the board with no undo history; finishing from there is recorded as a genuine win in causeway.wins (Won +1, deal check-mark, best moves/time). Run 2 banked a 29-second 'best time' for a 92-move deal after the demo played 64 of those moves. showSolution() already protects the daily tiers (it clears challengeDay - verified: after the assisted win of #10,004 the Daily card still showed Bronze unearned and all streaks 0), so the Wins store is simply missing the same guard. Careful with the obvious fix: refusing to record any win after a demo would also punish a player who stops the demo at move 1 and genuinely solves the deal, and it changes already-persisted best-times semantics. Suggest tainting the game only while assisted moves remain on the board (clear the taint on Replay/new deal), or recording assisted wins without a time/moves best.

tap Deal # pill, tap the text field, Select All, type 10004, tap Play

findings.note: NOT a behaviour bug - I read Game.swift. isSafeAutoplay() (Game.swift:576-585) is deliberately stricter than FreeCell: a card only goes home once BOTH opposite-colour neighbours (rank-1 and rank+1) are already resolved on a foundation, because Causeway tableau piles build in both directions so even an Ace can be a needed base. The behaviour is sound; the LABEL is the problem. 'Auto-play: On' is the only string the user ever sees - the How to play sheet (Extras.swift RulesView: Goal / The catch / Tableau / Free cells / Controls / About) never mentions Auto-play or Auto-finish at all - so an exposed Ace with an empty foundation reads as 'auto-play is broken'. Two independent testers hit this in round 2 (qa-worker-1 reported the same AD case on a random deal). Cheap fix: name it what it is ('Auto-play safe moves: On') and/or add one line to How to play, e.g. 'Auto-play only sends cards that can never be needed on the tableau - tap any other card to send it yourself.' Note the trap: making Auto-play aggressive instead would remove real skill decisions and could strand a deal, so do not 'fix' the rule.

findings.note: GameClock is a 1 Hz Timer, so suspension stops it and only the persisted integer `elapsed` is restored: switching apps is a free pause button, and recordWin() stores clock.elapsed as the best time (Game.swift:752). Measured precisely: 20 s foreground = +20 s (twice), but 23.7 s spanning a 20 s background = +6 s. TRAP: this is the same metric family as the deliberately-kept ux/Main:clock-runs-during-modal-sheets (commit 2796867 chose continuous timing for honest best-times); the consistent fix is a wall-clock anchor recomputed on foreground, but that also charges the player for phone calls/interruptions, and it retroactively changes what a 'best time' means. Human call - do not silently flip it, and if it is fixed, make sure a restored anchor cannot double-count the already-persisted elapsed.

measurements.measurement_method: column pitch measured off the 3x screenshot, +/-2pt

findings.note: The landscape branch's comment (ContentView.swift:44-51) says moving the toolbar into a rail and the cells under the foundations 'frees vertical + horizontal room so the cards grow'. Measured, they do not: cardW is width-constrained by widthCardW = (geo.width - 12 - railW 118 - 13*gap - 20)/12 (line 71), which on iPhone 17 Pro landscape (geo.width ~756pt after the 2x59pt safe-area insets) yields ~45pt - identical to portraitCardW (45pt) - while heightCardW would allow ~54pt. Net effect: rotating to landscape gains the player nothing in card size and leaves a 116pt (29%) empty band under the tableau. Structural (the 12-card-width three-column split is the cause), so routed as a proposal rather than a patch.

findings.note: Heuristic latency finding: screenshots at ~160ms cadence can only see stalls, not dropped frames. Most of the cost is UIDocumentPicker's first-use warm-up inside the app process (it recurs after every cold launch, not just once per install), so the app cannot make it fast — but it can show a spinner / disabled state, or pre-warm the picker. Double-tapping during the stall was tested and is harmless (only one sheet is presented). Everything else measured in this lane was fast: cold launch to painted board <=0.9s, Daily/Wins/How-to-play sheets settle in ~1.0-1.1s, New game redeal settles in ~1.65s.

findings.note: Testability, not user-visible. WORKFLOWS.md Fixture policy already names this gap and puts the proposal in scope. Suggested shape: a DEBUG-only launch argument (e.g. -causewayDayIndex N / -causewaySeed N) read once at startup, so daily streak/tier rollover becomes reproducible. Trap: any override that persists into a Release build would let a player farm daily streaks — it must be #if DEBUG and must not write to the daily record store.
